transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-06-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nandakumar (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood CSM), Marcus Nguyen (Cobalt ML), Elena Park (Cobalt Platform), Samir Patel (Cobalt SRE), Tina Cho (Cobalt Product)

Summary:
High-level console walkthrough focusing on request hop-map (span correlation), error analysis patterns, KV-cache miss visibility, and how to reproduce/triage model fallback paths. Customer wants concrete steps to run a targeted bench, and to understand data residency and audit logs for compliance.

Topics covered:
- Hop-map visualization (request -> model shard -> fallbacks)
- Trace retention & sampling strategy
- Prefix/KV cache miss analysis and optimization suggestions
- Error breed categories: tokenization errors, OOMs, quantization fallthroughs
- RBAC/SAML and KMS integration questions

Resources shared:
- Console hop-map demo recording: https://app.redwood.ai/console/demos/hop-map
- Quickstart trace export template: https://redwood.ai/docs/trace-export-template.csv
- Security playbook snippet (shared): /shared/security/SOC2-summary.pdf

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: all right thanks everyone for joining, um we're gonna run through the console hop-map and a couple of common failure patterns that customers hit when they have mixed hosted and dedicated usage. um, Priya and I will bounce back and forth.
[00:18] Marcus: cool, yeah thanks Jordan, we've had a few incidents where the model switched mid-request and produced truncated responses, so we're really hoping to see the tracing end-to-end.
[00:27] Priya: yep, great example. that often shows up as a span boundary in the hop-map - you'll see the request go to a primary model node then a fallback node, or sometimes a different quantized variant. we'll pull up a sample trace and annotate.
[00:45] Elena: quick Q — when you say fallback is that the "variant" fallthrough or is it more of a regional reroute? we've seen both.
[00:53] Priya: good question. both are possible. the hop-map differentiates by the reason code on the span: e.g. "capacity_unavailable" (region/burst) vs "inference_error" (model-level). sometimes the transcriber labels the reason slightly off, like it might say "inference err" in the short view.
[01:15] Jordan: i can share a console screenshot after but let's open a live trace — this is an anonymized trace Cobalt sent earlier, priy a can you start the playback?
[01:24] Priya: sure. loading trace... okay you can see the waterfall on the left, and the hop-map on the right. the hop-map uses parent-child spans — note the dashed lines, those are async hops like cache lookups.
[01:40] [screen share noise] 
[01:44] Priya: here's the first interesting bit: KV cache miss at 00:37 in the trace, there's no cached prefix so the request goes full path to the model shard. that's why tokens jump up in CPU time.
[02:03] Samir: hm we saw that spike in our metrics, we couldn't correlate it to a trace. Does the console link to the metric timeline?
[02:10] Priya: yes it does — in the trace detail pane there's a 'link metrics' toggle. sometimes the metric names come back with slightly different prefixes depending on ingestion (e.g., "redwood.request.latency" vs "rwd.req.latency"), so search with wildcard.
[02:30] Marcus: can you explain how you show KV cache misses vs prefix cache misses? we have both in our infra.
[02:36] Priya: sure. we emit two span annotations: cache.type = kv or cache.type = prefix, and cache.hit = true/false. in the UI we map those to icons, but the transcription occasionally has 'k v' as separate letters so the auto-summarizer sometimes munges it.
[02:55] Elena: also, are you sampling traces? we don't want full retention because of PII, but we need enough to cover regressions.
[03:02] Jordan: right — by default hosted includes 7 days of full traces at 1% sampling and 14 days at 100% for errors > 5% SLA breach. enterprise/private deployments can customize retention and sample rates.
[03:20] Tina: how do you anonymize traces? that's important for us.
[03:25] Priya: we automatically strip user_text fields when the redaction toggle is on, and we can pattern-match PII via regex rules provided by customers. also KMS keys can be customer-managed in Private.
[03:40] Marcus: walk us through an actual error path — the one that truncated responses.
[03:46] Priya: yep. here's the second segment: you see a span where tokenizer throws a "tokenize_error" then the runtime retries with a different tokenizer shim and that produces a shorter output. the hop-map shows a sibling span labeled "fallback: tokenizer_shim_v2".
[04:07] Jordan: sometimes those tokenizer errors are actually upstream — e.g., a malformed prompt from the app. we recommend instrumenting request validation earlier in the pipeline.
[04:20] Marcus: ok makes sense. any way to detect malformed prompts automatically?
[04:25] Priya: we have a rule engine in Optimize that can flag outlier tokenization rates and feed them into alerts, but you can also add a pre-filter in your edge.
[04:36] [05:02] Speaker 4: (inaudible)
[05:10] Priya: back to the trace — notice the span tags include model.version and kernel.quant. when the hop-map shows a quantized kernel being used, you can cross-check quality diffs. we recommend keeping quantized variants pinned to canary routes first.
[05:33] Elena: does the console surface model-level quality regressions or only perf metrics?
[05:39] Priya: both. there's an Eval correlation view — if you attach prompt-sets we compute BLEU/ROUGE-like diffs and flag regressions when generations deviate beyond a threshold. it's not perfect for open-ended tasks but it helps for structured outputs. (word unclear: "b-lue" sometimes transcribed as "blew")
[05:58] Marcus: about the hop-map visualization — can we export it as JSON? we'd like to feed it into our internal incident tool.
[06:05] Jordan: yes, there's a trace export button. it exports a flattened set of spans with trace_id and parent_id and reason_code. we'll share the export schema after the call.
[06:20] Priya: note that if you're on Dedicated and have VPC peering, the export includes an obfuscated node id, not internal IPs. privacy preserved.
[06:33] Samir: we have concerns around audit logs and SSO. how long do you keep admin audit trails?
[06:39] Jordan: hosted has 90 days by default for admin audit logs, enterprise/private can extend with S3 archival and HSM-backed KMS. we can provide the SOC2 artifact and the KMS integration guide.
[06:55] Elena: please send that.
[07:00] Jordan: will do.
[07:05] Marcus: earlier you mentioned capacity_unavailable fallbacks — do those generate a different alert channel?
[07:12] Priya: yes — capacity fallbacks are tagged as severity "warning" and can be routed to an on-call channel; inference errors are "critical". you can map them to PagerDuty or webhooks.
[07:24] [07:34] Priya: switching to a deep-dive example: this trace shows a request that got split into multiple shards due to sequence length after tokenization — one shard hit an OOM, triggered a fallback to a smaller context model, and the final reply lost trailing instructions. the hop-map shows the shard failure and the subsequent reroute.
[07:54] Marcus: is it possible to replay that exact request locally in our env? we want to reproduce.
[08:00] Priya: yes, use the trace replay tool in the console — it packages the request with the same model.version, tokenizer id, and input segments, but note that we obfuscate any customer PII unless you're in Private with BYOK.
[08:17] Elena: curious about costs — the shard + fallback path generates extra tokens. do you surface token-level cost per span?
[08:24] Priya: yes, each span includes token_count and estimated_cost which is computed using the active pricing profile at the time of the request. if you switch to Dedicated, you see committed vs burst token accounting.
[08:38] Marcus: that will help justify optimizations, thanks.
[08:43] Jordan: quick aside — some customers see spike patterns from batch aggregation when concurrent requests align; the hop-map will show a cluster of simultaneous root spans. you can tune autoscaling and batching window in the runtime.
[09:00] Samir: about sampling — what's the overhead of 100% tracing?
[09:05] Priya: it adds modest overhead; our runtime keeps trace recording as an async op to limit tail latencies, but storage costs rise. we usually advise 100% error tracing and selective 5-10% full trace sampling for production.
[09:23] Marcus: any gotchas with on-prem deployments? we've got strict egress policies.
[09:28] Jordan: for Private you can run the collector in-network and send envelopes to the Private control plane; no egress required if you opt for air-gapped mode. we have an on-prem deployment guide — will share.
[09:45] [10:09] Priya: demoing one more pattern: false-positive tokenization errors where a preprocessor strips invisible unicode and later tokenizer can't align spans. solution is consistent normalization at the edge and adding a deterministic hashing to input metadata as a quick check.
[10:30] Elena: can we add a rule in Optimize to auto-suggest normalization?
[10:35] Priya: yes, Optimize can suggest a normalization step and add it to the canary pipeline via the rollout API.
[10:50] Marcus: switching to security specifics — KMS, the key rotation schedule, and audit trail export.
[10:58] Jordan: hosted uses our KMS by default, rotation every 90 days; enterprise can plug in AWS KMS or HSM. audit trail export runs to your S3 with retention policy you set, and we provide proof-of-possession logs.
[11:15] Samir: is there a SOC2 cert we can attach to procurement?
[11:18] Jordan: yes we'll attach the SOC2 Type II, and the redacted pen-test summary.
[11:27] Tina: procurement will want encryption-at-rest details.
[11:31] Jordan: that's in the guide I'll send.
[11:35] [12:00] Priya: last demo bit — I'll simulate a runbook: detect error > open trace > identify span with reason_code > export trace > trigger replay > run local repro. i'm going to run it now on an anonymized trace.
[12:15] [screen share, trace replay running] 
[12:25] Priya: replay succeeded, response matches shortened output as expected. i flagged the tokenizer shim fallback in the trace and added a note in the trace comment field. you can attach runbook steps directly as actions on the trace.
[12:45] Marcus: that's super helpful — can we integrate those actions into our JIRA?
[12:50] Jordan: webhook integration available, you can push trace actions to JIRA tickets. we'll share the webhook schema.
[13:05] Elena: one last question — do you surface KV cache hit rates across regions in the console?
[13:11] Priya: yes, there's a per-region cache heatmap and a global aggregate. if you click a region it drills into node-level stats and sample traces.
[13:25] Marcus: okay, on next steps we need the export schema, pricing spreadsheet, SOC2 doc, and a bench script.
[13:33] Jordan: noted — I'll send the docs. Priya you'll run the bench.
[13:38] Priya: yep, I'll schedule the bench run; Elena, please upload the sample traces.
[13:45] Tina: thanks everyone.
[13:48] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts and book the simulation. bye.

End of meeting.
